abort_build.doc: Attempt to abort a build task. Only succeedes if task is currently abortable. Can provide either a build processor or container. Container requires a build task.

buildprocessor.doc: Build processor. Takes precedence over 'container' If 'buildtask' is provided, it must be the current build for this processor. If not provided, the current build is aborted.

abort_called_scripts.doc: Abort scripts that were called by this script on a global interrupt. No further interrupt actions will run after this action and this script will resume at the current label. This action is only allowed in global interrupt actions, not in library actions.

resume.doc: Label to resume at after the interrupt. By default the script will resume at the current label.

abort_scripts.doc: Abort all running AI scripts on an entity.

accept_offer.doc: Create the accept event for the mission offer cue which is waiting for 'event_offer_accepted'

vDoc.8.00: Create the accept event for the mission offer cue

activate_job_ship_orders.doc: Trigger the orders for this ship's job to start

activate_mission.doc: Activate an existing mission associated with a cue

activate_platform_trigger.doc: Activate a platform trigger (e.g. a button or certain doors)

result.doc: True if the activation succeeded or is not necessary, false if it failed (this can happen if the deactivating animation is currently running; wait a short time and retry)

stance.doc: Stance ID from libraries/stances.xml. Also needs to be in the ship macro's list of supported stances.

activate_ship_stance_by_tag.doc: Select a ship's stance using all specified tags and activate it

tags.doc: Specification tag or list of tags

activate_transporter.doc: Activate a transporter to schedule the movement of the contained entities, as well as the entities in the destination transporter

entity.doc: The entity who is intended to be transported. If not present in the transporter, the action will fail. This entity is also flagged as the 'triggerer' of the transport process.

result.doc: (optional) List of all entities successfully scheduled to move from the start transporter to the destination

activate_waiting_job_ship.doc: Inform the job engine that a waiting ship is ready for use

primary.doc: Set to true if it's a primary, false if it's a secondary group

add_actor_to_post_location.doc: Move the NPC actor to its default location for its control post

add_actor_to_room.doc: Add NPC actor to a room. This action fails if the actor could not be connected to that room.

blend.doc: Allow the NPC to blend their current animation to the triggered one (defaults to false)

chairtrigger.doc: Activation state for the chair if the slot is a chair slot (defaults to 'activate_chair'. Using 'invalid' will keep the chair in it current activation state)

object.doc: Room (or object with valid 'position') in which to place the actor (Not to be combined with 'slot')

result.doc: Whether the actor was successfully added

setroomslot.doc: Set the roomslot of the actor to the provided slot if it is a valid NPC slot (defaults to true)

slot.doc: The slot to place the actor (Takes precedence over 'room')

triggeranimation.doc: Trigger the default animations for this room slot on the actor (defaults to true)

add_ammo.doc: Add ammo to a defensible object (see also <remove_ammo> and <deplete_ammo>) NOTE: when used with unit macros storage limits are ignored! Use <add_units> instead!

amount.doc: Amount to be added (can be negative)

add_anomaly_destination.doc: Add an anomaly as a set destination of another. The destination will be picked at random on transition.

add_blueprints.doc: Add blueprints to player's blueprint library

cycle.doc: Cycle efficiency for blueprint(s) (will be the same for all added blueprints, uses 1.0 if not supplied)

flags.doc: Include blueprints for equipment in specific loadout elements (used only with object attribute, default is all loadout elements)

macros.doc: Macro or list of macros for which to add blueprints (can be combined with wares and object in a single call)

method.doc: Production method for blueprint(s) (will be the same for all added blueprints, uses default method if not supplied)

modules.doc: Include blueprints for modules (used only with object attribute, default is true)

object.doc: Object (station or ship) for which to add blueprints (can be combined with wares and macros in a single call)

product.doc: Product efficiency for blueprint(s) (will be the same for all added blueprints, uses 1.0 if not supplied)

resource.doc: Resource efficiency for blueprint(s) (will be the same for all added blueprints, uses 1.0 if not supplied)

wares.doc: Ware or list of wares for which to add blueprints (can be combined with macros and object in a single call)

add_boarding_attacker.doc: Add an attacker to the boarding operation and configure their behaviour and use of marines

add_boarding_pod_to_operation.doc: Add an approaching boarding pod to the boarding operation

add_build_to_construct_ship.doc: Add a build task to construct a ship

buildobject.doc: Existing object to be built as a new object

loadout.doc: Loadout value or Loadout ID (must be valid in 'macro' or the macro of 'buildobject')

macro.doc: Macro to build (overriden by the macro of buildobject if provided)

object.doc: Container object that has a build module

result.doc: Name of the value that will receive the result

add_build_to_expand_station.doc: Add a build task to expand a station

constructionplan.doc: Construction plan ID string or constructionsequence value

object.doc: Container object that has a build module

result.doc: Name of the value that will receive the result

add_build_to_modify_ship.doc: Add a build task to upgrade or restock a ship

ammo.doc: Table of ammo types (ware or macro) with assigned amounts

buildobject.doc: Existing object to be upgraded or restocked

immediate.doc: Start this order immediately? (Optional, defaults to false.) If true, the order is inserted as the current order. If there is an active current order, it will be interrupted, so that it restarts when the new order is completed. If the current order cannot be interrupted (i.e. it's in the critical state) the new order is inserted right after it. This attribute has no effect when creating a default order.

loadout.doc: Loadout ID (must be valid in the macro of 'buildobject')

object.doc: Container object that has a build module

result.doc: Name of the value that will receive the result

units.doc: Table of unit types (ware or macro) with assigned amounts

add_build_to_rebuild_fleet_ship.doc: Add a build task to rebuild a fleet ship

object.doc: Container object that has a build module

result.doc: Name of the value that will receive the result

add_build_to_recycle_ship.doc: Add a build task to recycle a ship

immediate.doc: Start this order immediately? (Optional, defaults to false.) If true, the order is inserted as the current order. If there is an active current order, it will be interrupted, so that it restarts when the new order is completed. If the current order cannot be interrupted (i.e. it's in the critical state) the new order is inserted right after it. This attribute has no effect when creating a default order.

object.doc: Container object that has a build module

result.doc: Name of the value that will receive the result

add_build_to_recycle_station.doc: Add a build task to recycle a station

object.doc: Container object that has a build module

result.doc: Name of the value that will receive the result
The resulting amount that was successfully added

add_clothing_mod.doc: Add clothing mod to an NPC or the player

entity.doc: The NPC or player that should receive clothing mod.

ware.doc: Clothing mod ware (from clothingmods.xml, defines a quality level and visual properties of a clothing mod)

add_commission.doc: Add price commission for target faction to object/faction(=target gets bonus pay for sales), if object and faction are specified, object takes precedence!

amount.doc: Discount/commission amount as percentage of a ware's price variation range, valid range from 1 to 100. NOTE: This is not the actual discount/commission percentage, which depends on the ware that the price modifier is applied to. Discounts/Commissions apply to all sell/buy offers of object/faction respectively.

name.doc: Name of commission, only required if target is faction.player

time.doc: How long this commission lasts. Will last forever if omitted!

add_conversation_view.doc: Add a dummy conversation action (<add_npc_line> without NPC voice) to trigger the conversation manager. Legacy, used only to prevent a small delay if a conversation ends without voice (e.g. when cancelled).

add_data.doc: Add data to a collectable, crate or lockbox

audiolog.doc: Audio log entry id or a list of audio log entry ids (ignored if timeline attribute is provided, one of the two must exist)

timeline.doc: Timeline entry id or a list of timeline entry ids (overrides audiolog attribute, one of the two must exist)

add_default_production_wares.doc: Add default wares to a ship or station based on its productions and buildmodules

extremechance.doc: Chance per ware that an extreme (0 or max) value will be added (ignoring the lower/upper limits) (optional)

add_discount.doc: Add price discount for target faction to object/faction(=target gets stuff cheaper), if object and faction are specified, object takes precedence!

amount.doc: Discount/commission amount as percentage of a ware's price variation range, valid range from 1 to 100. NOTE: This is not the actual discount/commission percentage, which depends on the ware that the price modifier is applied to. Discounts/Commissions apply to all sell/buy offers of object/faction respectively.

name.doc: Name of discount, only required if target is faction.player

time.doc: How long this discount lasts. Will last forever if omitted!

add_effect.doc: Add an effect object. If the effect's duration is infinite (value of -1), you need to remove it yourself with remove_effect.

object.doc: Object to attach the effect to

statechanges.doc: Should state change effects be applied to the object? (default is false)

add_encyclopedia_entry.doc: Add an entry to the encyclopedia (blueprints and spaces are not supported)

item.doc: Encyclopedia entry item ID (must be used together with type attribute, cannot be used together with value attribute)

type.doc: Encyclopedia entry type (must be used together with item attribute, cannot be used together with value attribute)

value.doc: Value from which encyclopedia type and item are derived (cannot be used together with type and item attributes)

add_equipment_mods.doc: Add one or more equipment mods to a ship

object.doc: Ship to add the equipment mods to.

add_holomap.doc: Add a holomap to a rendertarget

name.doc: Name of the value that will receive the result

rendertarget.doc: Name of render target on which the cutscene should be played (ignored for event monitor cutscenes)

add_holomap_text.doc: Adds a text label to the holo map. The text will be displayed below the icon of the reference component if the icon is visible, until <remove_holomap_text> is used. This only works if the map is active!

color.doc: Defines the text color in the format [r, g, b, a] - default is white [255, 255, 255, 255]

text.doc: Text string (does not suport line breaks)

add_inventory.doc: Add inventory to an entity (entity defaults to player, amount defaults to 1)

add_licence.doc: Add licence to a faction (defaults to player faction)

licence.doc: Licence to add (takes precedence over 'licencefaction' and 'type' pair)

licencefaction.doc: The licence issuing faction. Ignored if 'licence' is provided

type.doc: Type of licence. Ignored if 'licence' is provided

add_long_range_scan_effect.doc: Add a long-range-scan result effect object. Use this in reaction to <event_long_range_scan_sent> to get the distance-based timing to be correct.

color.doc: Optional color library entry to use

object.doc: Space or object used for positioning

add_mad_score.doc: Adds the attacker's MAD Weight to the target's MAD Score (ignores any limit)

attacker.doc: Attacker can either be a ship, a module of a station, or any of their sub-components

target.doc: Target can only be a ship or any of its sub-components

add_mass_traffic_quota.doc: Add a quota to a zone's main mass traffic network. Must supply either a macro, a ship group, or a job ID. If no end time is supplied you need to store it and stop the quota when you no longer need it.

amount.doc: The amount of ships in this quota

end.doc: The station where the mass traffic ships should end

endtime.doc: The time the quota should end (defaults to never if not supplied)

group.doc: Ship group for random macro selection

job.doc: Job ID for random macro selection and ship setup

quota.doc: (optional result) ID of the created quota

start.doc: The station where the mass traffic ships should start

starttime.doc: The time the quota should start (defaults to now if not supplied)

add_money.doc: Add money to a collectable or crate

add_npc_line.doc: Add an NPC voice line to the conversation

check.doc: Check for errors resolving an object name or description? Default is true

hidechoices.doc: Hide the player's conversation choices until after the NPC line has been spoken? Default is false (don't hide). This has no effect if the choices were already visible before the start of this line.

lookat.doc: Look in the direction of the specified component

recipient.doc: Recipient of the line, i.e. the character being spoken to (optional). Pass an NPC if this is a background speech between two NPCs. Default is the player (if omitted or null).

singleline.doc: If multiple text IDs are provided (either in sub-nodes or as a script list), should they be treated as a single NPC line? Otherwise they are treated as individual lines, as if they were added in separate <add_npc_line> actions. When the player skips a conversation line with a hotkey, this flag determines whether all of the contained lines are skipped instead of just a single line. Default is false.

speaker.doc: Speaker (optional, either an entity or a list [controllable_context, npc_template], defaults to the conversation actor if not supplied)

topic.doc: Topic of the line, i.e. the character being spoken about (optional). Pass an NPC or the player if the person being spoken about may have a grammatical effect on the sentence.

constantvel.doc: If set to true, the object will keep the new velocity indefinitely without accelerating/decelerating.

add_online_mission_reward_to_inventory.doc: Add reward inventory wares for an online mission to the online venture inventory and/or the player inventory. Online venture inventory items will be uploaded to the server. For such items, this action should only be performed shortly before the mission is completed, and not more than once per mission, otherwise successful upload of the provided online items is not guaranteed. Any other items will be added to the player inventory analogous to <add_inventory>.

wares.doc: Table of inventory wares (key = ware, value = amount to be added)

add_paint_mod.doc: Add paint mod to a ship

object.doc: Ship to add the paint mod to.

ware.doc: Paint mod ware (from paintmods.xml, defines a quality level and visual properties of a paint mod)

add_player_choice.doc: Add a player choice text to the conversation. When chosen, <event_conversation_next_section> will be triggered but the conversation stack will not be changed.

choiceparam.doc: Optional parameter that is passed to <event_conversation_next_section>. Can be of any data type.

add_player_choice_return.doc: Add a player choice text to the conversation. When chosen, the current sub-conversation will return to the previous section that started it (see <add_player_choice_sub> and <add_player_choice_subconv>), and <event_conversation_returned_to_section> will be triggered. This action also defines the behaviour of the "Back" button.

returnparam.doc: Optional parameter that is passed to <event_conversation_returned_to_section>. Can be of any data type.

add_player_choice_sub.doc: Add a player choice text to the conversation. When chosen, <event_conversation_next_section> will be triggered, and a sub-conversation will be started which can return to this section (see <add_player_choice_return>).

baseparam.doc: Optional parameter that is evaluated immediately, but stored until the sub-conversation returns and <event_conversation_returned_to_section> is triggered. Can be of any data type.

choiceparam.doc: Optional parameter that is passed to <event_conversation_next_section>. Can be of any data type.

add_player_choice_subconv.doc: Add a player choice text to the conversation. When chosen, <event_conversation_started> will be triggered, and a sub-conversation with a different actor will be started which will return to this section when it ends (unless the player aborts the conversation as a whole).

baseparam.doc: Optional parameter that is evaluated immediately, but stored until the sub-conversation returns and <event_conversation_returned_to_section> is triggered. Can be of any data type.

convparam.doc: Optional parameter that is passed to <event_conversation_started>. Can be of any data type.

add_player_commission.doc: Add price commission for player faction to object/faction(=target gets bonus pay for sales), if object and faction are specified, object takes precedence!

amount.doc: Discount/commission amount as percentage of a ware's price variation range, valid range from 1 to 100. NOTE: This is not the actual discount/commission percentage, which depends on the ware that the price modifier is applied to. Discounts/Commissions apply to all sell/buy offers of object/faction respectively.

name.doc: Name of commission, only required if target is faction.player

time.doc: How long this commission lasts. Will last forever if omitted!

amount.doc: Discount/commission amount as percentage of a ware's price variation range, valid range from 1 to 100. NOTE: This is not the actual discount/commission percentage, which depends on the ware that the price modifier is applied to. Discounts/Commissions apply to all sell/buy offers of object/faction respectively.

applytoshipsales.doc: Should this discount additionally apply to ship sales/upgrades? (defaults to false)

name.doc: Name of discount, only required if target is faction.player

time.doc: How long this discount lasts. Will last forever if 0 or omitted!

add_player_gravidar_access_request.doc: Add a request for access to the object's gravidar to be granted to the player

result.doc: The newly added region

add_relation_boost.doc: Add relation boost (otherobject or faction attribute required)

add_room_to_dynamic_interior.doc: Add a new room to a dynamic interior

check.doc: Check that any created room is suitable to be added to an interior which can support multiple rooms (e.g. the room has has no window connections). Set to false if the assets are assured to work together. Defaults to true.

door.doc: Door macro slot or connection name within corridor

interior.doc: Interior to add the room to

name.doc: Name of the value that will receive the result

add_scenario_stat.doc: Add a scenario stat to be shown in the debriefing menu

description.doc: The description, shown as a tooltip - useful to explain how the score is calculated if it's not completely obvious

id.doc: The ID string for this stat, must be unique inside a scenario

maxscore.doc: The "maximum" value for this stat's score (it's allowed to exceed it, the UI will show that state correctly) - if not set, the maximum value will be the total score required to reach 5 stars

name.doc: The name of this stat for display in the UI, preferably as a text ID string

score.doc: This stat's contribution to the total score - can be negative (omit if you don't want to show a numerical score and progress bar, also needs uivalue if this is set)

uivalue.doc: The value of this stat, formatted for display in the UI (omit if you don't want to show a numerical score and progress bar, also needs score if this is set)

add_skill.doc: Add skill value to either 'entity' or a npctemplate on 'object'

add_space_location_tag.doc: Add a location tag to the specified space

space.doc: Containing space (zone, sector, cluster, or galaxy)

add_stock.doc: Add inventory to a given entity using the entity's stock ID, as defined in the character definition.

entity.doc: The entity that should receive some stock.

add_supplies.doc: Add supplies to an object. NOTE: if the supplies are not needed to fulfill any current supply orders an attempt will be made to transfer them to storage, respecting stock limits!

add_supply_order.doc: Add supply orders to an object

description.doc: The description of this project that is shown to the player (text reference).

duration.doc: The time between all resources being delivered and the project completing.

name.doc: The name of this project that is shown to the player (text reference).

price.doc: The price of this project in Credits. Is used to calculate the full ware amounts, using the maximum possible prices, if a ware list is supplied.

pricescale.doc: The price scaling method. Defaults to 'absolute'.

repeat.doc: The minimum time between a project completing successfully and it becoming available again. The project is not repeatable if this is not set.

starttime.doc: The time this project was started. If supplied, the effects are already assumed to have taken effect. Defaults to "never".

successchance.doc: The success chance of this project in percent. Defaults to 100.

postfix.doc: Optional ID postfix, must be used when adding multiple projects based on the same library entry.

starttime.doc: The time this project was started. If supplied, the effects are already assumed to have taken effect. Defaults to "never".

successchance.doc: The success chance of this project in percent. Defaults to 100.

add_to_group.doc: Add an object or a list/group of objects to a group (the group is created if it does not exist yet)

check.doc: Produce an error message if an inserted object or list element is not an existing object? (default is true)

checkoperational.doc: Only add objects whose state is operational? (default is false) This will make sure that no existing but non-operational objects will be added, such as wrecks. Note: when an object is destroyed and possibly becomes a wreck, it is automatically removed from a group, so groups usually do not contain wrecks. However, without this attribute, adding a wreck to a group is still possible as long as it still exists in the universe. Note: non-existing objects cannot be added to a group anyway, and attempting to add an invalid object may still result in an error message unless check="false" is used.

group.doc: Group of objects to add to the group (cannot be used with attributes object or list)

groupname.doc: Name of the group to which the result will be added (group will be created if it does not exist yet)

list.doc: List of objects to add to the group (cannot be used with attributes object or group)

object.doc: Object to add to the group (cannot be used with attributes list or group)

replace.doc: Replace all existing group members with the object(s) supplied (default is false) Note: consider using this instead of using <clear_group> first when repopulating group, to avoid overhead of removing and re-adding the same objects. Note: can be used even if the group does not already exist. Note: order of members in the group may be different when using this, with previously-existing members first followed by new ones.

add_tolerance_boost.doc: Add tolerance boost (otherobject or faction attribute required)

add_trade_subscription.doc: Add permanent player subscription to trade offer updates of the specified object. This also immediately adds the current trade offers to the trade memory.

duration.doc: How long this subscription is valid for. Unlimited duration if omitted. (optional)

add_tradeware.doc: Add trade ware (use only on trading stations)

allowbuy.doc: Allow buying this tradeware (optional, defaults to true)

allowsell.doc: Allow selling this tradeware (optional, defaults to false)

lockavgprice.doc: Lock price to average price of ware, otherwise price is calculated based on storage amounts (optional, defaults to false)

ware.doc: Single ware or list of wares that should use the same settings

vDoc.8.00: Ware

add_units.doc: Add units to an object (either 'macro' is to be provided or both 'category' and 'mk')

faction.doc: The faction that made the units - defaults to the owner of the object if not provided

unavailable.doc: Add the unit as currently unavailable (default = false)

add_ware_reservation.doc: Reserve space for selling ware to an object.

amount.doc: Positive number of units to reserve.

duration.doc: Duration of this reservation (optional, defaults to 1 hour)

mission.doc: Whether the reservation is for a mission trade (optional, defaults to false)

object.doc: The container where the reserver(object) wants to reserve space for an amount of ware.

replace.doc: Whether amount should be added to any existing reservation or replace it. (optional, defaults to false)

reserver.doc: Which object to reserve this amount for.

result.doc: The amount that is now reserved for this reserver. Can be different from amount if there already was a reservation. (optional)

supplies.doc: Whether to check reservations for "supplies" (optional, defaults to false)

virtual.doc: Whether to look at the "real" or the "virtual" dataset - virtual reservations are IGNORED for trades. (optional, defaults to false)

result.doc: Whether everything was added successfully

add_watchdog_units_to_masstraffic.doc: Add watchdogs units of a station to its zone's masstraffic

add_weapon_to_weapongroup.doc: Adds a weapon to the specified weapon group.

primary.doc: Set to true if it's a primary, false if it's a secondary group.

add_workforce.doc: Add workforce of the specified race to a given object. (will not add more than can fit, see $container.workforce.{$race}.capacity)

add_yield_reservation.doc: Reserve enough yield from a resource area to fill this ship's cargo space

resourcearea.doc: The resource area to which to add the reservation

advance_seed.doc: Changes the numerical seed value for fixed random number generation in a consistent way, based on the previous seed value. Can be used to generate a sequence of random numbers starting with a single numerical seed value. NOTE: This should only be used for numerical seeds, not when using an object as seed source. An object seed is advanced automatically when using it to generate a random number.

seed.doc: The numerical seed value to be updated

allow_conversation_escape.doc: Allows or disallows escaping from the current conversation section (e.g. with Esc). Only the current section is affected, default is allow.

enabled.doc: Should Escape be possible in current conversation section?

animate_chair.doc: Animate a chair to suit the using NPC

actor.doc: The NPC using or set to use the chair

chairtrigger.doc: Activation state for the chair (defaults to 'invalid')

delay.doc: (optional) delay the animation by the specified amount of time

slot.doc: The NPC slot related to the chair

append_list_elements.doc: Append elements from list 'other' or component group 'group' at the end of a list

create.doc: Should the list be created if it does not exist yet? (Default is false)

group.doc: Group whose members will be appended (cannot be used together with 'other')

name.doc: Name of the list to which the elements of the other list (or group) will be appended (if the 'create' attribute is true and the list does not exist yet, then this value will receive the newly created list)

other.doc: List whose elements will be appended (cannot be used together with 'group')

reverse.doc: If true then the elements of the other list are appended in reverse order (defaults to false)

append_to_list.doc: Append an element at the end of a list

create.doc: Should the list be created if it does not exist yet? (Default is false)

name.doc: Name of the list to which the element should be added (if the 'create' attribute is true and the list does not exist yet, then this value will receive the newly created list)

unique.doc: Should the element not be appended if it is already contained in the list? In that case, the existing list will remain unchanged. (Default is false)

apply_attackstrength.doc: Apply damage from an attack to target, returns if target was killed

explosion.doc: Is the damage explosive? Uses different low attention parameters such as 'surfaceelementexplosivechance' and equally damages a selected surface element and object hull.

hullnoshield.doc: Attack strength to be applied to hull only if no shields are present (ignored if total supplied).

hullonly.doc: Attack strength to be applied to hull only (ignored if total supplied).

hullshield.doc: Attack strength to be applied to hull and shields (ignored if total supplied).

module.doc: Attack a specific module of the object (optional, defaults to a random operational module, if there are any, or the object as a whole otherwise.)

shielddisruption.doc: Shield disruption value of this attack (defaults to 0)

shieldonly.doc: Attack strength to be applied to shields only (ignored if total supplied).

strength.doc: Approximate total attack strength as a single value (individual values ignored if supplied).

surfaceelement.doc: Attack a specific surface element of the object (optional, defaults to a random operational surface element of the module/object, if there are any.)

apply_construction_sequence.doc: Appends a construction plan to a station that already exists. The construction plan for the station can be empty.

remove.doc: Remove any existing module that is not part of the provided sequence (defaults to false)

sequence.doc: A construction sequence or construction plan ID

station.doc: The station to which the construction sequence should be attached. This station must already be connected to the gamegraph, otherwise use create_station action.

apply_experience.doc: Apply experience to either individual 'entity' or crew aboard 'object' (identified by npctemplate for an individual crew member or role for a group )

apply_influencelist.doc: Apply an influencelist (as defined in influenceconfigurations) to 'object'

allowstop.doc: Allow this influence to be stopped by calling <stop_script_influences>. Note that this will stop all influences created from scripts with allowstop set to true, regardless of the influence list ID.

influencelist.doc: Influence list definition ID (string. defined in libraries/influenceconfigurations.xml)

object.doc: Object to apply the influences to

apply_loadout.doc: Apply the specified loadout to an object or construction sequence at the specified index.

flags.doc: Loadout flags for elements to apply, and operations (add/remove) to perform.

index.doc: The index of the entry in the sequence to which the loadout that should be applied. Must be supplied if sequence is also supplied.

loadout.doc: The loadout that should be applied.

object.doc: Object to apply the loadout to. Either a ship, or a station module.

sequence.doc: A sequence to which the loadout should be applied. If sequence is given, index must also be given, as a loadout is applied to a specific entry in the sequence.

apply_player_influence.doc: Apply change to player influence value

influence.doc: Influence value change (can be positive or negative, result will be restricted to valid range)

assert.doc: Evaluates the value and prints an error message if it does not match. This requires the script debug filter to be enabled, both at game start and on the assert. (In developer builds a modal message box will pop up, and there is no filter requirement.)

break.doc: Determines on how many assertion failures the message box may pop up (default is 1). Note that resetting or refreshing the MD resets the counter.

text.doc: Message text to be displayed on assertion failure

assign_construction_vessel.doc: Assign a construction vessel to work for a build module of a build storage. Construction vessel is not yet deployed to aid in building.

assign_control_entity.doc: Assign NPC actor as the control entity for the specified control post of the specified object

init.doc: Start the suitable AI scripts on the actor. (defaults to true)

result.doc: Was the NPC sucessfully assigned?

transfer.doc: Move the actor to the object's control room instantly. (defaults to false)

assign_diplomacy_ship.doc: Assign a ship to assist a diplomacy agent

ship.doc: The ship to assign. Ships docked at the player HQ will be stored and change owner to civilian.

assign_dismantling_target.doc: Make a claim on an object to dismantle (also related to dismantle/tow claims from other object)

assign_hired_actor.doc: Assign NPC actor (hired by player) as the control entity for the specified control post, or as a crew member with the specified role, on the specified player-owned object. If the assignment is possible, <event_player_assigned_hired_actor> is triggered and a success is indicated, otherwise a failure reason is provided. The actual assignment logic is implemented in an MD event handler. If the check value is set to true, the assignment via the event is skipped, so this action has no effect and only indicates success or failure.

actor.doc: Actor entity (NPC) or list containing context and NPC template

check.doc: Only check for expected outcome (with attributes success and/or failed), without actually performing the assignment? Defaults to false.

failed.doc: Optional name of the value that will receive the failure reason string, or null if successful

post.doc: Control post (either post or role must be specified)

role.doc: Actor (entity) role (either post or role must be specified)

success.doc: Optional name of the value that will be set to true if successful, false in case of failure

target.doc: Player-owned controllable target object on which the actor is assigned to a control post or role (may be the actor's currently assigned object)

assign_order_syncpoint_to_order.doc: Assign a sync point to an AI order. Sync point must have been created previously with <create_order_syncpoint>. The AI order must be an infinite order in the queue (not a default order), and it may not have entered the critical state or the finish state yet.

order.doc: AI order to which the existing sync point should be assigned

owner.doc: AI order that is the owner of the sync point

assign_tow_target.doc: Make a claim on an object to tow (also related to dismantle/tow claims from other object)

attach_component_to_interior.doc: Attach a component to an interior (for internal use only)

interior.doc: Interor to attach to (must be of class room or navcontext)

name.doc: Name of the value that will receive the result

attach_object_to_target.doc: Attach an object to the target using the 'limpet' connection (only supported on ships so far)

keepoffset.doc: Whether the currect offset of object relative to target should be kept, uses target center otherwise (defaults: true)

benchmark_start.doc: Enable Benchmarking (until we call benchmark_stop) Note: This action is only available in egosoft-internal builds with benchmarking enabled

directory.doc: Sub-folder of the personal folder where the benchmarking results will be stored (optional)

benchmark_stop.doc: Disable Benchmarking (has to be previously started with benchmark_start) Note: This action is only available in egosoft-internal builds with benchmarking enabled

blur_screen.doc: Blurs the screen to a certain strength over time.

duration.doc: The duration of the interpolation period from the current blur value to the specified 'strength'

holdtime.doc: The duration over which the screen should remain blured. (defaults to indefinite)

strength.doc: The blur value at the end of the interpolation duration (1.0 is maximum blur)

break_formation.doc: Break formation as a formation leader. No effect if the object is not a formation leader

can_process_recyclable_object.doc: Checks whether a recyclable object can be processed in a processing module

result.doc: Will receive true if processing is possible, otherwise false

trade.doc: The trade(offer or deal) associated with selling recyclables to a station with a processing module.

can_safely_extend_build_plot.doc: Can the build plot be extended without encroaching on other plots or static objects?

cancel_all_orders.doc: Cancels all existing AI orders in the object's order queue

cancel_conversation.doc: Cancel an active conversation (if providing a conversation actor, the conversation is only cancelled if the actor matches)

conversation.doc: Optional conversation name. If supplied then the conversation is only aborted if the conversation name matches.

force.doc: Should conversation be aborted even if Escape was explicitly disabled via <allow_conversation_escape>?

cancel_cue.doc: Cancel cue. This only takes effect after the current cue actions have been performed. For more details, see section "Cleaning up instances explicitly" in the Mission Director Guide.

cancel_order.doc: Cancels an AI order and removes it from the owner object's order queue. NOTE: If the order is in the critical state, it will not be cancelled. Instead, a <event_object_order_cancelled> will be sent with immediate="false", which is a request that may or may not be handled by the order script (see documentation of orderstate.critical).

keepinloop.doc: In case of a cancelled loop order, keep the cancelled order in the loop instead of removing it? This only has an effect if the order is part of an order loop and is not temporary. Any other order is not affected by the attribute and will be removed anyway. This attribute is useful for cancelling the current order, for the purpose of finishing its execution in a safe way and proceeding to the next order.

cancel_space_reservation.doc: Cancels a reservation of a reserving component in a specific zone.

index.doc: Index of the reservation, must be specified.

zone.doc: Zone that was used to create the reservation, i.e. the value holding the "safezone" that was provided by the action creating the reservation.

capture_movie_start.doc: Start capturing a movie (to stop capture, see capture_movie_stop)

capture_screen.doc: Make a screenshot (optional in a subdirectory)

directory.doc: Sub-folder of the personal screenshot folder where the screenshot will be stored (optional)

excludedweaponmode.doc: All weapons/turrets should stop firing except when in this mode (if omitted, there is no exception) If weaponmode specifies one particular mode it has precedence over excludedweaponmode unless weaponmode and excludedweaponmode are identical in which case this action does nothing.

staydeployed.doc: Should weapons/turrets stay deployed if they already are? (defaults to false)

weaponmode.doc: All weapons/turrets in this mode should stop firing. (defaults to any)

center_holomap_view.doc: Center the camera on the known bounds. This only works if the map is active!

instant.doc: Whether the position and/or zoom level should be set instantly; if set to false the camera pans and/or zooms smoothly (defaults to false)

zoomtofit.doc: Whether the camera should also zoom in/out to fit the known bounds, within allowed limits (defaults to false)

change_relation_on_attack.doc: Change relation of the attacked object towards the attacker

result.doc: This value will be set to true if there was an effect on the relation (or at least the relation boost decay), otherwise it is set to false. The action can fail in several cases, e.g. if attacker and victim are of the same faction.

change_relation_on_boarding.doc: Change relation of the boarded object towards the boarder

allowfactionrep.doc: Allow the faction reputation between the boarded and boarder factions to change if possible (defaults to true)

attempt.doc: Is this a boarding attempt or the end of a successful boarding operation?

result.doc: This value will be set to true if there was an effect on the relation (or at least the relation boost decay), otherwise it is set to false. The action can fail in several cases, e.g. if attacker and victim are of the same faction.

change_relation_on_kill.doc: Change relation of the killed object towards the killer

result.doc: This value will be set to true if there was an effect on the relation (or at least the relation boost decay), otherwise it is set to false. The action can fail in several cases, e.g. if attacker and victim are of the same faction.

check_age.doc: Game age value is in specified range (both value and range can use time expressions)

check_animation_state.doc: Check if a matching animated part is currently in the specified animation state

group.doc: The group ID (which may be a string or a tag) of the animated part

result.doc: Whether the actor was successfully added

tag.doc: A tag (which may be a string or a tag) to help find the part connection

check_is_area_obstructed.doc: Check if a ship is inside the designated area. Ignores mass traffic (as long as it's in the lane) and ships that have collision avoidance currently disabled (due to docking or parking).

name.doc: Name of the value that will receive the result

check_is_build_location_free.doc: Check if a build location is free. Takes highways and objects like stations and gates into account, but ignores ships or asteroids.

name.doc: Name of the value that will receive the result

check_is_position_inside_boundingbox.doc: Check if a position is inside an object's bounding box

name.doc: Name of the value that will receive the result

check_job_active.doc: Check if the specified job is currently active

result.doc: Name of the value that will receive the result

check_line_of_sight.doc: Check if object has line of sight to the target (uses ray casts)

excludeself.doc: Exclude object from raycast check. True by default. Can be used in conjunction with objectoffset or targetoffset to check if specific relative position has line of sight.

name.doc: Name of the value that will receive the result

objectoffset.doc: Offset relative to the object from where the line of sight check is performed.

targetoffset.doc: Offset relative to the target to which the line of sight is checked.

useaimtarget.doc: If set to true, an object's aim targets (or the bounding box center if there are none) will be used as the raycast target, consistent with weapon aiming. If false, the coordinate center will be used. Defaults to false.

result.doc: Name of the value that will receive the result

check_production_allowed.doc: Check if a production for a specified ware is allowed to be added to an object

result.doc: Name of the value that will receive the result

usemaxlimits.doc: Check against the max limits defined in the module definition, otherwise use the base limits. (defaults to true)

check_value.doc: Value is in specified range (both value and range can use expressions)

value.doc: Value to match (checked for non-zero if no comparison range or list is specified)

check_walk_path.doc: Check whether a NPC can walk do a destination

checkstate.doc: Check if the NPC is currently able to move. NPCs can not move if in low attention or are hidden. (defaults to true)

destination.doc: The ultimate destination component. Used to judge which surfaces the NPC may be alowed to walk on. (if 'end' is the the destination, this is not necessary)

destinationtags.doc: Known floor tags at the destination position. Used to judge which surfaces the NPC may be alowed to walk on.

end.doc: Object or component slot destination. Combined with 'end' position.

result.doc: Name of the value that will receive the result

start.doc: Object or component slot to start from. Combined with 'start' position. (optional, NPC uses current position if not provided)

check_weapon_active.doc: Check whether the weapon is currently active

result.doc: Name of the value that will receive the result

check_weapon_installed.doc: Check whether the weapon is installed/available

result.doc: Name of the value that will receive the result

claim_ship.doc: Claim the target ship using pilot. ATTENTION: this moves 'this' to $target! All further this.* calls will correspond to $target!

faction.doc: Faction that will take owership of ship. Will default to ownership of pilot controllable if omitted.

pilot.doc: Pilot that will do the claiming. Will be moved from its current controllable to target if provided.

target.doc: Ship that will be claimed. Must be ownerless.

clamp_equipment_amount.doc: Clamp wares and amounts of ordered ammunition, units, and deployables depending on resources available to the builder

ammo.doc: Table of ammunition or deployable wares with assigned amounts to be clamped

builder.doc: The object that is building the new equipment

object.doc: The object that is getting the new equipment

resultammo.doc: Resulting table of ammo wares and amounts clamped to what the builder has enough resources to build. Will return null if attribute ammo is not populated.

resultunits.doc: Resulting table of unit wares and amounts clamped to what the builder has enough resources to build. Will return null if attribute units is not populated.

units.doc: Table of unit wares with assigned amounts to be clamped

clamp_trade_amount.doc: Clamp trade amount value based on buyer/seller storage situation (bundle/unbundle states are taken into account and the appropriate storages - cargo, ammo or units - are checked)

amount.doc: Initial amount to clamp based on buyer/seller storage limits (optional, defaults to 2147483647)

bundle.doc: Should the ware be bundled (convert ammo/unit -> ware) on transfer? (optional, defaults to the trade offer bundle flag)

buyer.doc: The buyer to look at for free storage limitations (optional, either buyer or seller must be specified)

reason.doc: If amount was reduced, contains a string indicating which restriction reduced it to the lowest value. Possible values are 'seller_cargo', 'buyer_cargo' or 'buyer_money'. Null if amount remains unchanged.

result.doc: Amount clamped so it matches how much seller has and how much buyer can store and afford.

seller.doc: The seller to look at for stored item limitations (optional, either buyer or seller must be specified)

unbundle.doc: Should the ware be unbundled (turn ware into ammo/units) on transfer? (optional, defaults to the trade offer unbundle flag)

updatedeal.doc: Should the passed-in tradedeal amount be updated if the clamp results in a reduction of amount? (optional, defaults to false, DO NOT USE FOR TRADE OFFERS!)

clear_actor_current_chair.doc: Clear the current chair of this actor (NPC actors only)

clear_actor_emotion.doc: Clear an actor's emotion morph target

clear_actor_pod_arrival_time.doc: Clears the scheduled time of arrival for an actor (hired by the player). If an arrival time was previously set on the actor, this triggers the arrival at the current object. See <set_actor_pod_arrival_time>.

actor.doc: Actor entity (NPC) or list containing context and NPC template

clear_actor_roomslot.doc: Clear the current roomslot of this actor

clear_actor_tool.doc: Remove a currently held tool from the actor

lefthand.doc: False to use right hand (default), true to use left hand

vDoc.8.00: false to use right hand (default), true to use left hand

lefthand.doc: False to use right hand (default), true to use left hand

vDoc.8.00: false to use right hand (default), true to use left hand

clear_buildanchor.doc: Clear the buildanchor of the specified buildprocessor

buildprocessor.doc: Build processor to clear the buildanchor of

clear_buildmethod_override.doc: Clear any build method override on an object, the object will revert to inheriting the default settings.

clear_collision_filter.doc: Clear the list of objects for which collisions are disabled

clear_dismantling_target.doc: Clear the dismantling target of an object

wreck.doc: The object set to be dismantled

clear_entity_role.doc: Clear the role of an actor (entity)

clear_entity_role_object.doc: Clear the role object of an actor (entity)

clear_faction_diplomacy_exclusion.doc: Clear the faction diplomacy exclusion reason(s) between these two factions

flags.doc: Diplomacy exclusion reason flag list (use as many as required, space-separated)

clear_fleet_ship_build_issues.doc: Clear build issue flags for the fleetunit

fleetunit.doc: Fleetunit of an existing controllable to be restored

clear_fog_of_war.doc: Clear the fog of war in a radius around a given position. Does not reveal any objects.

sector.doc: The sector in which to reveal the fog of war.

clear_group.doc: Clear a group, i.e. remove all members from it (note: consider using <add_to_group> with replace="true" instead if repopulating group, to avoid overhead of removing and re-adding the same objects)

group.doc: Group of objects

clear_list.doc: Clear a list (equivalent to resizing to 0 elements)

clear_npc_template_role.doc: Clear the role of a npc template

clear_object_access_licence.doc: Clear licence restriction for access to object or space

clear_object_description.doc: Clear an object's description and revert to default

clear_object_friend_foe_list.doc: Clea friend/foe list of a mine that supports this (mine will revert to using faction relations)

object.doc: The mine whose foe list should be cleared

clear_object_name.doc: Clear an object's name and revert to default

clear_object_sound_override.doc: Clear an object's override sound. Currently only room ambient sounds are supported.

clear_order_failure.doc: Mark a currently running AI order as not failed, if it has previously failed via <set_order_failed>. If there is a failure record for the order in the order system UI, it is removed as well. If the order is a default order, any failure record of a previously running default order on the object is also cleared, no matter if the current default order has failed or not. Note: If the order was restarted after failing, it does not count as failed any more, and a recorded failure from before the restart cannot be removed with this action, except for default orders.

clear_player_firstperson_override.doc: Clear the player's first person movement override

clear_player_target.doc: Clears the player's current HUD target.

clear_recurring_order_failure.doc: Removes the failure record for a failed recurring queue order of the provided order ID from the order system UI, if there is one. In case the matching failed AI order is still currently running, it is marked as not failed. This action has no effect on recorded failures of non-recurring or non-queue orders.

clear_ship_undocking.doc: Resets the state of the ship's dockingbay from 'undocking'. Has no effect if the current state is different.

clear_shortage_reports.doc: Clear the object's reports of wares which are either in short supply, insufficient or overflowing

clear_table.doc: Clear a table, i.e. remove all keys and values from it

clear_tow_target.doc: Clear the tow target of a ship, releasing its claim on the target object

object.doc: The object set to be towed

clear_visitor_as_mission_object.doc: Clear relation between a visiting object and its assigned MD mission

collect_asteroid.doc: Have an asteroid be instantly collected by a ship

collect_deployable.doc: Have a deployable be instantly collected by a ship

collect_drop.doc: Have a drop be instantly collected by an object

collect_unit.doc: Have a unit be instantly collected by an object

commandeer_object.doc: Commandeer an object to be used by faction logic

complete_diplomacy_action_operation.doc: Trigger the diplomacy action operation to complete

complete_diplomacy_event_operation.doc: Trigger the diplomacy event operation to complete with a certain outcome

outcome.doc: The ID of the operation outcome (required if the operation event has outcome options defined)

connect_player_to_scenario_console.doc: Connect the player to the specified scenario console slot

activate.doc: Open the scenario selection menu, otherwise leave the position after connecting. (defaults to true)

triggeranimation.doc: Trigger the animation moving the player to the slot position, otherwise instantly connect. (defaults to true)

connect_to_trade_location.doc: Connect a ship to a trade location (= reserve parking space) If result is null then the operation failed.

result.doc: Name of the value that will receive the result

continue.doc: Skip the current iteration of the innermost <do_while>, <do_for_each> or (counted) <do_all> loop, and continue with the next iteration.

count_clusters.doc: Count matching clusters and check if count is in specified range

groupname.doc: Name of the group to which the result will be added (group will be created if it does not exist yet)

Since it takes a lot of CPU time to calculate the result, the action is completed instantly and the result will be provided later via <event_object_construction_sequence_created>. To retrieve the result immediately as part of the action, use the child element <immediate>, but be aware that it will block the rest of the game until the result is available.

Normally a failure only occurs by reaching the timeout (if timeout attribute is present) or if the input to the generator does not allow for enough flexibility (e.g. if no connectors are supplied or the plot size is too small). To prevent failure, the remaining unconnected modules will be added in free space without any connections. default.doc: Create as default order of the object? (Optional, defaults to false.) Instead of being added to the order queue, the order will replace the previous default order.

immediate.doc: Start this order immediately? (Optional, defaults to false.) If true, the order is inserted as the current order. If there is an active current order, it will be interrupted, so that it restarts when the new order is completed. If the current order cannot be interrupted (i.e. it's in the critical state) the new order is inserted right after it. This attribute has no effect when creating a default order.

name.doc: Name of the value that will receive the result

override.doc: Is this an override order? (Optional, defaults to false.)

priority.doc: Is this order inserted and executed as a priority order? (Optional, defaults to false.) If there are no priority orders in the queue already, this order will get inserted as the current order (like an immediate order). Otherwise, it will get inserted after the last existing priority order in the queue. Special behaviour of priority orders can be implemented by checking the priority flag of the currently running order. NOTE: Priority orders are not guaranteed to be at the start of the order queue. Immediate orders are always inserted at the start of the queue, no matter if they are priority orders or not. This attribute has no effect when creating a default order.

create_order_syncpoint.doc: Create an AI-controlled sync point that is owned by an AI order. The AI order must be an infinite order in the queue (not a default order), and it may not have entered the critical state or the finish state yet. The sync point is automatically assigned to the owning AI order, and remains assigned as long as the order exists. The sync point is removed completely (including all order assignments) when either the owning order is completed/removed or the sync point gets unassigned from it (see <unassign_order_syncpoint_from_order>).

edit_order_param.doc: Changes an order parameter, as if edited by the player in the UI. Note that this has side effects for already running orders and can fail in some cases. If the order is in the started state (non-critical), it will be reset and start over. If in the critical state, any <editable> actions will be performed and <event_order_param_edited> will be triggered. You can check with "$order.isparameditable.<param>" whether a param is currently editable. Editing a param fails if: (1) the order is in the critical state and the param has no <editable> node that allows editing, or (2) the order is the default order or in a critical state and the param decides whether the order is infinite (i.e. it has an infinitevalue), or (3) the order is in the finish state.
